history.summary: Plan r1 complete: P1–P11 (generator fixes, publish, three judgment-layer phases, Architecture, then the R4/R6 push sweep split by push class under D1), a shared push-sweep attachment, and 15 criteria in verification.json. Two questions in plan_questions_r1.md: Q1, P7 (Architecture) cannot pass its gate here because Architecture's gates need the modern-app toolchain this environment lacks (recommend adding it and restarting before the run); Q2, R2's redis edge does not fall out of the existing wiring as settled, because an image-level upstream hard-fails (recommend letting the container scoping cover the wire too; the plan is written that way).

Plan r2: rulings D3 and D4 applied to the r1 plan. P7 now gates through modern-app after the operator's pre-run restart, and is blocked if the tool is missing. P2/P5 scope the upstream wire per container and keep its hard fail (V03 records that). The sidecar notes no longer assume it is stale or fresh. Citations re-verified at unchanged heads, and the dry run parses all 11 phases.

The criteria, targets and code citations hold. Three findings: nothing says what happens when slice 027's unpushed commits sit in this slice's target repos (operator); the carrier search and V12 rely on a GitHub code search that returns 10 of the carriers; P5's gate runs the pod's pre-P2 generator. Two advisories: the 2-hour executor cap during the sweep, and sweep pushes happen before review.

Plan r3 applies the review r1 rulings. P4 now checks for other slices' unpushed commits before the run's first push, publishes aac-tools and stops for the restart; P5 then checks the sidecar's --help (F1, F3). The carriers are listed with gitblit and proven with GitHub trees (F2, V12). The sweep is split into 10 phases sized from Jenkins build durations, each class opening with a canary (F4, F5). No carrier is a phase Target any more, so an archived HelmCharts is left alone. The dry run parses 18 phases.
